tools.name: dillie_whoami
tools.description: Asks the server who owns the current dillie session (name, email) and which workspace it is in (name, tenantId). Call this first when it is unclear whether you are authenticated before calling other dillie tools. Never exposes access tokens or other sensitive data. To filter tasks assigned to the signed-in user, pass assignee "me" to dillie_query_tasks — no userId lookup is needed.

tools.name: dillie_list_projects
tools.description: Lists dillie projects, optionally filtered by status or a name search term. Use it to find a project ID before working with a specific project. The id in the response is the identifier passed as the projectId argument of other tools.

tools.name: dillie_get_project
tools.description: Gets a project's details (name, description, status, owner, etc.) by project ID.

tools.name: dillie_create_project
tools.description: Creates a new dillie project. Its list is always provisioned in agile mode with the default issue types (initiative, epic, story, task, bug, subtask, e2e), an initiative/epic top-level hierarchy, and sprints enabled.

tools.name: dillie_get_project_resources
tools.description: Gets the IDs of a project's sub-resources (the task list's listId, root folder, overview canvas, channel, etc.). Call this first to get a listId before using task tools such as dillie_query_tasks. The IDs in the response are identifiers meant only as arguments to subsequent tool calls.

tools.name: dillie_list_members
tools.description: Lists a project's members, including user details. Use it to check that a user exists before specifying an assignee by name.

tools.name: dillie_list_fields
tools.description: Gets the field definitions of a task list (name, type, role, options, etc.). Use it to find the IDs of role-based fields such as assignee (ASSIGNEE) and status (STATUS), or the fieldIds to put in values when creating or updating a task.

tools.name: dillie_query_tasks
tools.description: Queries a project's tasks (list items) with filters, sorting and cursor pagination. If assignee is a member name, it is turned into a userId filter automatically in two steps: look up the member list, then look up the ASSIGNEE field ID. With topLevelOnly, only top-level (root) tasks are returned. The id of each item in the response is the itemId argument of follow-up tools such as dillie_get_task. For the signed-in user's own tasks, pass assignee "me".

listId.description: List ID (the listId returned by dillie_get_project_resources)

assignee.description: Assignee filter. Takes a member name or a userId (UUID). A name is resolved to a userId automatically by looking up the member list. For the signed-in user's own tasks, pass "me" — the server resolves it to the account that owns this connection. Do not guess the "current user" from project roles or the member list. To filter by a member whose name is literally "me", pass their userId.

sort.description: List of sort conditions. Each entry has the form "fieldId:asc" or "fieldId:desc".

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous result (to fetch the next page)

topLevelOnly.description: If true, returns only top-level (root) items

value.description: Value to compare against. A scalar for eq/neq/gte/lte/contains, an array for in; omit for isEmpty/isNotEmpty
Value to compare against. A scalar for eq/neq/gte/lte/contains, an array for in; omit for isEmpty/isNotEmpty

tools.name: dillie_create_task
tools.description: Creates a new item (task) in a task list. values maps fieldIds obtained from dillie_list_fields to values. With parentItemId, the task is created as a subtask. Set the issue type with the alias key values.issueType (an ISSUE_TYPE option id). In agile projects (every new project) the issue type is required and the server rejects a task without one with 400 — it does not pick one for you. A top-level task may only be an initiative or an epic, and a subtask only a type its parent's type allows; the allowed types are the project's hierarchy and topLevelAllowed.

parentItemId.description: Parent item ID (to create a subtask)

tools.name: dillie_update_task
tools.description: Updates an existing task's (list item's) field values, parent item (parentItemId) and color. values only needs the fieldId → value pairs to change. The previous values of the fields you pass are overwritten and cannot be restored. Completing or cancelling is done with dillie_complete_task or dillie_cancel_task, not this tool (the server rejects setting done directly).

parentItemId.description: Parent item ID (null moves the task to the top level)

tools.name: dillie_list_sprints
tools.description: Lists the sprints of a list (agile mode), in all states (FUTURE/ACTIVE/COMPLETED). The id in the response is the sprintId argument of the sprint tools.

tools.name: dillie_get_task
tools.description: Gets a single task by itemId (field values, issue key, parent item, sprint, whether it is sealed, whether it has children). `_description` in values is the raw Markdown description — for items stored as legacy HTML, dillie_get_task_description converts it to Markdown.

tools.name: dillie_get_task_description
tools.description: Gets a task's description as Markdown. Legacy HTML descriptions saved before the switch to Markdown are also converted to Markdown. An empty string if there is no description.

tools.name: dillie_set_task_description
tools.description: **Overwrites the entire** task description with Markdown (it does not append — the previous body is lost and cannot be restored). To add to it, merge your text into the original from dillie_get_task_description and pass the result. The server rejects HTML tags with 400.

tools.name: dillie_complete_task
tools.description: Transitions a task to a completed status (STATUS category completed). The server rejects setting done directly with dillie_update_task, so complete tasks with this tool. An idea (issue type idea) cannot be completed — accept it as a task with dillie_accept_idea first. With note, the note is posted to the task channel first and the transition runs only if that succeeds. undo=true reverts the completion; the reverted task goes to the first unstarted status, not back to its previous status.

undo.description: If true, reverts the transition. A reverted task goes to the **first unstarted status**, not back to its previous status — a reverted idea goes back to the Idea status.

note.description: Note to post to the task channel before the transition (Markdown). The message is posted first and the transition runs only if it succeeds — if the message fails, the status does not change. By default it is posted as the user's automation bot.

noteAsMe.description: If true, posts the note as the user themselves. The default (false) posts it as the automation bot, so text written by a tool is not recorded as if a person wrote it. Set true only when passing on text the user wrote themselves.

tools.name: dillie_cancel_task
tools.description: Transitions a task to a cancelled status (STATUS category cancelled). With note, the reason is posted to the task channel first and the transition runs only if that succeeds. undo=true reverts the cancellation; the reverted task goes to the first unstarted status, not back to its previous status, and a cancelled idea goes back to the Idea status. Cancelling an idea is how it is discarded.

undo.description: If true, reverts the transition. A reverted task goes to the **first unstarted status**, not back to its previous status — a reverted idea goes back to the Idea status.

note.description: Note to post to the task channel before the transition (Markdown). The message is posted first and the transition runs only if it succeeds — if the message fails, the status does not change. By default it is posted as the user's automation bot.

noteAsMe.description: If true, posts the note as the user themselves. The default (false) posts it as the automation bot, so text written by a tool is not recorded as if a person wrote it. Set true only when passing on text the user wrote themselves.

tools.name: dillie_accept_idea
tools.description: Accepts an idea (issue type idea, in the Idea status) as a task by changing its issue type to issueType and its status to the starting status in one step. Call this only after you have proposed which issue type to accept it as and where it belongs (including how to group child ideas) and the user has approved — never accept an idea on your own without the user's consent. If it belongs somewhere else, move it there first with dillie_update_task (parentItemId), then accept it as a type allowed at that place. An idea under another idea can only be accepted after its parent is accepted. An idea cannot be completed until it is accepted. The server rejects an item that is not an idea in the Idea status, an issue type that is idea or not an option, a list with no starting status, and a hierarchy violation.

issueType.description: ISSUE_TYPE option id to accept the idea as (from dillie_list_fields). Not idea; it must be a type the idea's current parent allows (topLevelAllowed when it is top-level) and must allow the types of its child items

annotations.title: Accept an idea as a task

tools.name: dillie_get_task_tree
tools.description: Collects a task and its subtasks recursively and returns them as a tree (each node has id, issueKey, title, status, issueType, children). status and issueType are replaced with option labels. depth counts the root (1 means the root only; the default is the whole tree).

itemId.description: ID of the task (item) to use as the root

depth.description: Maximum depth including the root (1–50). Default 50

tools.name: dillie_assign_task_sprint
tools.description: Assigns a task to a sprint (sprintId) or moves it back to the backlog (sprintId=null). The previous assignment is overwritten.

sprintId.description: Sprint ID to assign. null moves the task back to the backlog

annotations.title: Assign a task to a sprint

tools.name: dillie_get_project_stats
tools.description: Gets task statistics for **one** project (total counts and counts by status and by type, completion rate, progress per top-level task). This is not a cross-project summary — to cover several projects, iterate with dillie_list_projects and call it for each. The by-status and by-type keys are option IDs; get their labels from dillie_list_fields.

tools.name: dillie_create_sprint
tools.description: Creates a sprint in the FUTURE state in a list (agile mode). Start it with dillie_start_sprint.

tools.name: dillie_start_sprint
tools.description: Transitions a FUTURE sprint to ACTIVE. There is no tool to undo this. A list can have several ACTIVE sprints — starting is not rejected while another sprint is in progress, so if only one should run, check with dillie_list_sprints first. The server rejects sprints that are not FUTURE.

tools.name: dillie_complete_sprint
tools.description: Transitions an ACTIVE sprint to COMPLETED. There is no tool to undo this. Tasks that are not completed or cancelled are removed from the sprint and return to the backlog (sprintId=null). The server rejects sprints that are not ACTIVE.

tools.name: dillie_search_platform_docs
tools.description: Runs a hybrid search over the public Dillie platform docs (product guides and docs). When answering questions about platform features, usage or policies, base the answer on the excerpts and cite the url as the source. No sign-in required.

locale.description: Result locale (e.g. ko, en). Defaults to ko.

tools.name: dillie_platform_docs_nav
tools.description: Gets the nav tree of the public docs (hierarchy of sections and documents). Use each document's product and slug to read its full text with dillie_read_platform_doc. No sign-in required.

locale.description: Locale (e.g. ko, en). Defaults to ko.

tools.name: dillie_read_platform_doc
tools.description: Gets the full body (MDX) and frontmatter of a single public document by product and slug. Use it when search excerpts alone are not enough and the answer must rest on the full document. Get product and slug from the nav tree. No sign-in required.

locale.description: Locale (e.g. ko, en). Defaults to ko.

revision.description: A specific revision number. Defaults to the current revision.

tools.name: dillie_list_platform_docs
tools.description: Lists the public docs for a locale (and optionally a nav section) as a flat list (product, slug, title, section, navOrder). For the hierarchy use dillie_platform_docs_nav; for full text use dillie_read_platform_doc. No sign-in required.

locale.description: Locale (e.g. ko, en). Defaults to ko.

section.description: Filter by nav section path. Defaults to all sections
